title: Good slicing radius by Lebesgue differentiation and Markov (Simon 6.5.1, (8)–(10))
statement: Choice of a good slicing radius (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (8)–(10)). Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ, μ' be finite measures on ℝ^P (IsFiniteMeasure), f : ℝ^P → ℝ measurable, ρ > 0 real and B ∈ [0, ∞] with μ({x : f(x) < ρ}) ≤ B. Then there is r with ρ/2 < r < ρ such that liminf_{h → 0+} h⁻¹·μ({x : r − h < f(x) < r}) ≤ (4/ρ)·B and liminf_{h → 0+} h⁻¹·μ'({x : r − h < f(x) < r}) < ∞. Values are in [0, ∞]: h⁻¹ and 4/ρ are read through ENNReal.ofReal, and liminf is taken along the filter 𝓝[>] 0 of right neighbourhoods of 0.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (ρ : ℝ) (B : ℝ≥0∞), IsFiniteMeasure μ → IsFiniteMeasure μ' → Measurable f → 0 < ρ → μ {x | f x < ρ} ≤ B → ∃ r ∈ Ioo (ρ / 2) ρ, liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ {x | r - h < f x ∧ f x < r}) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (4 / ρ) * B ∧ liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ' {x | r - h < f x ∧ f x < r}) (𝓝[>] 0) < ∞
